record.context_brief: Optimal constant in the basic orthonormal inequality
record.original_question: Determine the optimal constant K_d in the orthonormal Sobolev/Lieb-Thirring inequality: for every N and every orthonormal family u_1, ..., u_N in H^1(R^d), find the best K_d such that sum_n ∫_{R^d} |∇u_n|^2 dx ≥ K_d ∫_{R^d} (sum_n |u_n|^2)^(1+2/d) dx.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. Find the optimal constant Kd in (1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 1$. For an integer $N \geq 1$, consider any orthonormal family $u_1, \ldots, u_N$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, i.e. $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} u_i \overline{u_j}\, dx = \delta_{ij}$. The orthonormal Lieb–Thirring (kinetic) inequality states that there exists a constant $K > 0$, independent of $N$ and of the family, such that
$$\sum_{n=1}^{N} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |\nabla u_n(x)|^2\, dx \;\geq\; K \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left( \sum_{n=1}^{N} |u_n(x)|^2 \right)^{1+\frac{2}{d}} dx.$$
Determine the largest such constant $K_d$, that is,
$$K_d \;=\; \inf \frac{\sum_{n=1}^{N} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |\nabla u_n|^2\, dx}{\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left( \sum_{n=1}^{N} |u_n|^2 \right)^{1+2/d} dx},$$
where the infimum is over all $N \geq 1$ and all orthonormal families $u_1, \ldots, u_N$ in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ (with the right-hand side nonzero). Find an explicit expression for $K_d$ in every dimension $d$.
artifact.status_search_result: The determination of the optimal (sharp) constant in the orthonormal Lieb–Thirring kinetic inequality remains a famous open problem. Recent work (Frank–Hundertmark–Jex–Nam, 2021) disproved the one-bound-state part of the original Lieb–Thirring conjecture for the dual eigenvalue formulation when κ > max(0, 2 − d/2), and the semiclassical constant is known to be sharp only for κ ≥ 3/2; the value of the sharp constant in the orthonormal H^1 form considered here is not known in any dimension.

status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress disproves the one-bound-state conjecture, but the sharp constant remains undetermined.
